[In English] stations," and I will not pronounce the name of the station, "shall jam only at the request of the PEB organ of the 2nd Corps and at the request of the Main Staff, OU, extension unknown, of the PEB department and never on one's own initiative [indiscernible] Sarajevo front." [Interpretation] Did you ever have the opportunity to see this order, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Isn't this an order that was sent to your unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. But there is a location indicated here. You can read it. Which is not -- maybe if we go into private session, I can refer to the names. It was not at the location where I was. This is something else. And I can explain that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In fact, there is another location but there also yours. There is also your facility, the southern facility; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But what you are talking about was being done by the communications unit in this other facility, which doesn't mean that we did it, too, at our facility. Because I said yesterday that when it came to jamming, we tried something but we never achieved much or anything of significance, and I always felt that this was counterproductive for us to jam the conversations that we wanted to monitor and record. The two things don't go together.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I would like the witness to be shown 5D150, Exhibit 5D150. Witness, I know that we are talking about jamming of conversations, and this is not at all the topic I am mainly interested in. However, there is a sentence which shows that this is a report stemming from your unit. If you could please look at the sentence that begins with "by the way," and then you can read as follows: "[In English] By the way, the transformer and we rectify which we borrowed from [indiscernible] operator." [Interpretation] I just assumed that there were two units at that facility, and if someone lent something from the communications unit, it can only be your own unit. Isn't that the case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible. It's possible. I'm not denying anything. I'm not claiming anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And I would like to ask you the following question. At the very beginning of the document, there is a question of equipment that was left by the UN. Could you please explain to us what this equipment is, what this is about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just read it for a minute. At the facility where I was working, to this day, there are systems or repeaters or digipeaters from the UN, from Samarstrof [phoen], from the electricity board. There is a special UN container, and they still have their repeater communications through that facility, so this was a generator that was theirs. I haven't read to the end. Maybe we used it briefly or linked up with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I would not like to put words in your mouth but could you please tell us what this abbreviation means, UN?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: United Nations. They had their representatives through -- during the war and they had their own communications, and they still have them and they are still operational.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And according to this document, if I understand correctly, you used some equipment that belonged to the United Nations; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We didn't use it. This was just the generator. But the equipment we didn't dare, nor did we have any need to use it. There must have been a short break in the power system, and the generator supplies the power. So this may have been an isolated case.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And tell us, the communications unit of the United Nations, was it placed there as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never, never. But if they needed to service the generator or to repair some antennas or something, they would come occasionally and do their work. I didn't interfere with that, nor did I have any need to, nor did I have any right to prevent anyone from doing such things.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perfect. Thank you, Madam Fauveau, for your cooperation. I take it, just for formality, Mr. Sarapa, you still maintain you don't need to cross-examine this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: No, we don't have any questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. And Mr. Josse you have already confirmed. So basically, sir, that means before we bring to an end -- do you have any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that means that we have brought your testimony to an end, and that's also thanks to the cooperation of all the lawyers in this room. I wish to thank you on behalf of everyone for having come over and given testimony, and also on behalf of everyone I wish you a safe journey back home. Our staff will give you all the attention you require and all the assistance you require to facilitate that. Thank you. And have a nice evening.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Tomorrow, just to confirm, because for a moment someone got my mind confused. We don't have another witness but Major Rutten tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We have another one available to follow on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but I think the understanding is that Major Rutten will engage us most of the day, if not all.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If that's correct, that's fine, but if we finish early we will have somebody available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So tomorrow morning it's a morning sitting. We have shifted from the afternoon to the morning. Okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Then, Your Honour, should we run through the numbers of the exhibits tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can do that tomorrow. I would rather not keep the staff any longer here. We can do it tomorrow morning, thank you. Unless I hear an objection. I hear no objections. Thank you. So good evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 7th day of December, 2006, at 9.00 a.m.
